newsitem.title: FRANCE: Grain tenders not on agenda for Thursday EU talks.
newsitem.headline: Grain tenders not on agenda for Thursday EU talks.

text.p: Grain export tenders do not figure on the agenda for Thursday's weekly European Union grain talks, member country officials said on Tuesday.
That is no guarantee that the European Commission will hold back from opening up stalled export tenders at Thursday's talks, but such a move is unusual without prior warning, the officials said.
The Commission's director general for agriculture, Guy Legras, said on Tuesday the EU was "not in a hurry" to open up the tenders, which are the main export channel for EU cereals.
The agenda for Thursday afternoon's cereals management committee meeting is stripped of all but a few routine end-of-month items, officials said.
Weekly grain exports are currently closed, while preferential imports of maize to Spain were fully allocated last week, so that item too has been dropped.
Rice tenders are open as usual, however.
The panel will be asked to set refunds for processed grain products, as it does at the last meeting of each month.
A meeting of the same group at expert level on Thursday morning will discuss those refunds and continue a technical discussion from last week on rules affecting rice.
